beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW - Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Bonjour, this is Liam, in for Bear. Today we tear down the screen dash clean skill. It is the shared preprocessor that turns a screen recording — Zoom, Teams, Meet, or QuickTime — into a beat that fits inside a reel. Five passes. One review artifact. Never publishes. Here is the mental model.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW - hesitant writer corrects the 'auto-blurs' misread to the actual mechanism 'flags'. Single-token trigger per BrutalistHesitantWriter contract.
beats.narration_text: The name reads like a cleaner. It is not one. The screen dash clean skill does not sanitize your desktop or decide what is embarrassing on your behalf. It runs five passes over the recording, applies safe defaults, and flags what a human still needs to look at. The proof of a good pass is not the number of pixels cropped. It is the contact sheet at the end.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST - the anatomy of screen-clean on disk. One file. Two callers.
beats.narration_text: First, the anatomy. On disk this is a small skill. One file — skills slash make slash screen dash clean slash SKILL dot md — the doctrine. That is it. What matters is who calls it. Fellows calls it. Guests calls it. Anything else that drops a recorded human into a reel calls it. The point of screen dash clean is not what it does. It is that it is one skill instead of two.

props.title: The screen-clean skill on disk.

beats.role_note: The pipeline - five passes from screen recording to cleaned beat + contact sheet.
beats.narration_text: The flow is five passes, and only one of them ever decides anything on your behalf. Pass one — probe the file and decode the audio. Pass two — aspect fit, measured against the taskbar, padded with cream bars, never cropped from the top. Pass three — legibility, sampled from real frames at output size. Pass four — privacy scan, which flags every incidental thing on screen and waits for a human. Pass five — dead dash air trim on the ends only. Middle edits are the caller's job, not this one's.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 - IGNORANT OF WHO IS SPEAKING. Shared preprocessor for fellows AND guests. Format is orthogonal to relationship.
beats.narration_text: First decision, and it is the whole reason this skill exists. screen dash clean is deliberately ignorant of who is speaking. It does not know whether the recording is a mentee or a board member or a guest. That relation belongs to the caller. What screen dash clean knows is pixels — a sixteen by ten capture, with a taskbar, carrying someone's whole desktop in frame. Split by format, not by relationship, and both callers get sharp output. Split by relationship instead, and one of them ships letterboxed frames — which, per the doctrine, is exactly the state fellows was in before this skill existed.

props.heading: Ignorant of who is speaking.
props.body: The editorial relationship (mentee vs. board member vs. guest) belongs to the CALLING skill, never here. screen-clean knows pixels: a 16:10 capture with a taskbar and someone's whole desktop in frame. Building the cleanup into fellows OR guests means the OTHER one ships letterboxed frames — which is where fellows was before this skill existed.
props.quote: Format is orthogonal to relationship. Anything that ingests a recording calls this.
props.cite: screen-clean SKILL.md · Why it is shared
props.sparkLine: The pixels are shared. The relation is not.

beats.role_note: Design decision 2 - Pass 1 audio gate. Decode with volumedetect; STOP at -40 dB. Real ffmpeg output on synthetic fixtures captured in demo/screen-clean-run.log.
beats.narration_text: Second decision. Pass one is a gate, not a check. screen dash clean decodes the actual audio — with ffmpeg dash a f volumedetect — and if the mean volume is below negative forty decibels, it stops. Not warns. Stops. Because the downstream stages will happily build a dead episode around a silent take. The doctrine is explicit — never infer audio from the presence of an audio stream. Decode it. On a long recording, sample a ninety second window from the middle so volumedetect stays fast.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 2 · PASS 1 lands

body: ffmpeg volumedetect · silent take = dead episode · 90s sample on long files
quote block lands verbatim from SKILL.md

props.heading: Decode the audio. Stop at -40 dB.
props.body: Real demo (demo/screen-clean-run.log): a 2560×1600 fixture with anullsrc measures mean_volume = -91.0 dB → STOP. The same fixture with a 440 Hz sine measures -21.1 dB → proceed. On a long recording, sample a 90-second window from the middle instead of decoding end-to-end — volumedetect stays fast.
props.quote: If mean_volume is below -40 dB, STOP. … Never infer audio from the presence of an audio stream — decode it.
props.sparkLine: Silent tape in. Dead reel out. Gate it.

beats.role_note: Design decision 3 - Pass 2 aspect fit. Three routes A/B/C. B (crop taskbar only) is the default. Cream bars, never black. Never crop from the top.
beats.narration_text: Third decision. Pass two solves the sixteen by ten problem without lying about it. A screen recording is sixteen by ten. A reel is sixteen by nine. Three routes. Route A — pillarbox, no crop, ninety six pixel bars each side, taskbar still on screen. Route C — full crop to sixteen by nine, no bars, but eighty eight pixels of shared content come off the bottom with the taskbar. Route B — the default — crop only the seventy two pixels of taskbar and pad the rest with cream bars. Nothing shared is lost. And the bars are Claude cream, never black. Black reads as a letterboxed upload. Cream reads as in dash register. And a rule that never bends — never crop from the top. The webcam thumbnail lives there. Every removed pixel comes off the bottom.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 3 · PASS 2 lands
heading 'Measure the taskbar. Pad the rest.' fades in
body: A/B/C table redrawn from SKILL.md · cream bars · never crop top
quote block lands verbatim from SKILL.md
verdict pill 'B — 72 px crop, 56 px cream bars'

props.heading: Measure the taskbar. Pad the rest.
props.body: For a 2560×1600 source: A = pillarbox, no crop → 1728×1080 with 96 px bars; C = full crop to 16:9 → 1920×1080 but ~88 px of shared content lost; B (DEFAULT) = crop the ~72 px taskbar only → 1809×1080 with 56 px cream bars, nothing shared lost. Bars are Claude cream #FAF9F5, never black — black reads as a letterboxed upload. And never crop from the top — the webcam thumbnail lives at y=0.
props.quote: Measure the taskbar. Do not assume it. … Bars are Claude cream #FAF9F5, never black.
props.verdictLabel: B — 72 px crop, 56 px cream bars
props.sparkLine: Cream, not black. Bottom, not top.

beats.role_note: Design decision 4 - Pass 4 privacy scan. Flag, never decide. 'Is this embarrassing' is judgment, not arithmetic.
beats.narration_text: Fourth decision, and this is the line the skill will not cross. Pass four is a privacy scan. screen dash clean lists every incidental thing it sees — clock, dock icons, browser tab titles, notification toasts, filenames, calendar previews. Then it marks which ones the taskbar crop already removes, and which ones survive into the reel. Then it waits. It does not auto blur. It does not decide. Is this embarrassing is a judgment call, not arithmetic. And the doctrine is explicit — this matters more for fellows, who are on personal machines with their own life on screen, than for board members who present deliberately.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 4 · PASS 4 lands
heading 'Flag. Never decide.' fades in
body: list surface · mark survives-crop vs. removed-by-crop · wait
quote block lands verbatim from SKILL.md
verdict pill 'judgment, not arithmetic'

props.heading: Flag. Never decide.
props.body: The scan lists: system clock and date · dock/taskbar icons and badges · browser tab titles · notification toasts · visible filenames and paths · calendar or mail content. Marks which items SURVIVE the crop and which the crop REMOVES. Then waits for a human. This matters more for fellows — personal machines, real life on screen — than for board members who present deliberately.
props.quote: Never auto-blur and never decide on someone's behalf — 'is this embarrassing' is judgment, not arithmetic.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY - The proof of Pass 2 is the CONTACT SHEET, not the numbers. Four frames sampled 10/35/60/85%. The shared screen changes.
beats.narration_text: Falsifiability. Numbers do not answer this question. Seventy two pixels cropped and fifty six pixel bars is not something a human can judge in the abstract. So after applying the default, the skill renders a contact sheet — four frames sampled across the recording at ten, thirty five, sixty and eighty five percent, each composited exactly as it will appear in the reel, bars included, saved as one PNG. Not one frame. Four. Because the shared screen changes over the recording. A crop that costs nothing while the speaker is on a web page can clip a terminal six minutes later. The human confirms on pixels, not on numbers.

props.heading: The contact sheet is the proof.
props.body: After Pass 2 applies the default, four frames are sampled across the recording (~10% / 35% / 60% / 85%), composited exactly as they will appear in the reel — bars included — and written as ONE PNG. Four, not one, because the shared screen changes. Numbers like '72 px crop / 56 px bars' are not something a human can judge in the abstract. Pixels are.
props.quote: The proof is the review artifact, not the numbers. … A crop that costs nothing while the speaker is on a web page may clip a terminal six minutes later.
props.sparkLine: Four frames. One decision. Human's call.

beats.role_note: VERDICT - artifact card. Six lines that recapitulate the skill.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. screen dash clean is the shared preprocessor for any skill that drops a recording into a reel. It is deliberately ignorant of who is speaking. Format is orthogonal to relationship. Pass one is a gate — mean volume below negative forty and the build stops. Pass two crops the taskbar, pads the rest with cream, and never touches the top of the frame. Pass four flags what is on screen and waits for a human. And the deliverable back to the caller is a cleaned nineteen twenty by ten eighty video plus a contact sheet you can actually look at. Small skill. Sharp job.

props.artifactHeading: A gate. A crop. A flag. A sheet.
artifactLines: Shared preprocessor called by fellows, guests, and anything else that drops a recording into a reel.
Pass 1 is a gate: decode the audio with ffmpeg -af volumedetect; if mean_volume is below -40 dB, STOP.
Pass 2 crops the measured taskbar (~72 px), pads with cream bars (#FAF9F5), and never touches the top.
Pass 3 samples real frames at output size; an illegible screen share is a finding, not a defect to paper over.
Pass 4 flags every incidental item on screen and waits for a human — never auto-blurs, never decides.
Delivers to the caller: cleaned 1920×1080 video + a four-frame contact sheet + a measured-numbers report.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW - Your Turn composer with a paste-ready dry-run prompt. Liam reads aloud and discusses. Safe: synthetic fixture only, no crop, no real recording.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Make a synthetic screen recording with ffmpeg — a solid grey rectangle at twenty five sixty by sixteen hundred, six seconds, silent — so nothing personal is at risk. Then follow the doctrine of screen dash clean's Pass one. Run ffprobe to record the container, video codec, audio codec, and dimensions. Run ffmpeg dash a f volumedetect and read the mean volume. If it is below negative forty decibels, print the STOP verdict and halt. Then reason out loud — with what you would show on screen for Pass two — the three A B C aspect routes, the number of pixels each removes, and the width of the bars in each. Do not run the crop. Do not touch a real recording. This is a doctrine dry run.
